title: Enable palm rejection on T2 MacBooks
author: marashiai
body:
## Summary

- classify the built-in T2 MacBook touchpad as internally integrated
- install the udev rule during fresh T2 hardware setup
- migrate existing T2 installations and request a reboot
- cover installation, migration, idempotence, and non-T2 exclusion in tests

## Why

The `t2bce` driver exposes the built-in keyboard and trackpad through a virtual USB bus. systemd therefore labels the touchpad as externally integrated, so libinput does not pair it with the internal keyboard for disable-while-typing. Palm contact can then scroll or move the pointer while typing.

The rule is limited to Apple `05ac:0340` event devices already identified as touchpads and changes only `ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION` to `internal`.

## Validation

- `udevadm verify default/udev/apple-t2-touchpad.rules`
- `bash -n install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh migrations/1786776556.sh test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh`
- `bash test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh`
- `git diff --check`
- verified on a 2019 Intel MacBook Pro with T2 (`linux-t2` 7.1.8): udev changed the built-in touchpad from `external` to `internal`

`./test/shell` reaches and passes the added T2 coverage. Its unrelated environment-dependent checks require the separate `omarchy-pkgs` checkout; the runtime smoke test also conflicts with the active desktop shell.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+# The T2 BCE driver exposes the built-in MacBook touchpad over a virtual USB
+# bus, causing systemd's input_id helper to classify it as external. Mark only
+# the touchpad interface as internal so libinput can enable disable-while-typing.
+#
+# The product ID varies by model: these are every WELLSPRINGT2 keyboard/trackpad
+# ID hid-apple binds to, which is the device the trackpad hangs off.
+ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="input", KERNEL=="event*", ENV{ID_VENDOR_ID}=="05ac", ENV{ID_MODEL_ID}=="0278|027[a-f]|0280|0340", ENV{ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD}=="1", ENV{ID_INTEGRATION}="internal", ENV{ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION}="internal"

@@ -19,6 +19,11 @@ if lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null; then
     echo "hci_bcm4377"
   } > /etc/modules-load.d/t2.conf
 
+  # The virtual USB bus makes udev mistake the built-in touchpad for an
+  # external one, preventing libinput from disabling it while typing.
+  install -D -m 0644 "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/udev/apple-t2-touchpad.rules" \
+    /etc/udev/rules.d/99-omarchy-apple-t2-touchpad.rules
+
   # linux-t2 7.1.4 replaced the apple-bce driver with t2bce; t2bce_vhci is the
   # virtual USB host controller the internal keyboard hangs off, and mkinitcpio
   # pulls t2bce_core/t2bce_dma in via module dependencies.

@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+echo "Enable palm rejection on T2 MacBook touchpads"
+
+if ! lspci -nn | grep "106b:180[12]" >/dev/null; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+source_rule="$OMARCHY_PATH/default/udev/apple-t2-touchpad.rules"
+rule=/etc/udev/rules.d/99-omarchy-apple-t2-touchpad.rules
+
+if [[ -f $rule ]] && cmp -s "$source_rule" "$rule"; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+sudo install -D -m 0644 "$source_rule" "$rule"
+
+# Libinput must reopen the device to pick up its new integration type.
+omarchy-state set reboot-required

@@ -7,6 +7,8 @@ source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
 fix_t2="$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh"
 other_packages="$ROOT/install/omarchy-other.packages"
 migration="$ROOT/migrations/1785944594.sh"
+touchpad_rule="$ROOT/default/udev/apple-t2-touchpad.rules"
+touchpad_migration="$ROOT/migrations/1786776556.sh"
 
 grep -Fq 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" intel_iommu=on iommu=pt pm_async=off mem_sleep_default=deep"' "$fix_t2" ||
   fail "T2 setup installs the suspend kernel parameters"
@@ -20,6 +22,19 @@ grep -Fq 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" intel_iommu=on iommu=pt pm_async=off mem_sl
   fail "T2 setup leaves optional Touch Bar customization uninstalled"
 ! grep -qx 'tiny-dfr' "$other_packages" ||
   fail "the ISO no longer caches tiny-dfr"
+grep -Fq 'ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION}="internal"' "$touchpad_rule" ||
+  fail "T2 touchpad rule enables libinput disable-while-typing"
+grep -Fq 'ID_INTEGRATION}="internal"' "$touchpad_rule" ||
+  fail "T2 touchpad rule sets systemd's canonical integration property"
+grep -Fq 'ID_VENDOR_ID}=="05ac"' "$touchpad_rule" &&
+  grep -Fq 'ID_MODEL_ID}=="0278|027[a-f]|0280|0340"' "$touchpad_rule" &&
+  grep -Fq 'ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD}=="1"' "$touchpad_rule" ||
+  fail "T2 touchpad rule covers every T2 keyboard/trackpad and nothing else"
+grep -Fq 'install -D -m 0644' "$fix_t2" &&
+  grep -Fq '99-omarchy-apple-t2-touchpad.rules' "$fix_t2" ||
+  fail "fresh T2 setup installs the touchpad integration rule with fixed permissions"
+grep -Fq '106b:180[12]' "$touchpad_migration" ||
+  fail "T2 touchpad migration is limited to T2 hardware"
 pass "fresh T2 setup uses t2bce-compatible suspend, fan, and Touch Bar defaults"
 
 test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)

reviews.body: ## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. Adds support for correctly classifying Apple T2 MacBook touchpads as *internal* so libinput can enable disable-while-typing (palm rejection), for both fresh installs and existing systems via a migration. **Changes:** - Add a udev rule to mark the affected Apple T2 touchpad interface as internal. - Install the udev rule during fresh T2 setup and add a migration to apply it on existing T2 machines. - Extend the T2 hardware shell test to validate rule content and installation/migration gating. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh | Adds assertions ensuring the new udev rule and migration are present and properly scoped. | | migrations/1786776556.sh | New migration that installs the udev rule only on T2 hardware and marks reboot required. | | install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh | Installs the udev rule as part of the fresh T2 setup path. | | default/udev/apple-t2-touchpad.rules | New udev rule that tags the Apple T2 touchpad as internal for libinput behavior. | --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.




<details>
<summary>Suppressed comments (2)</summary>

**migrations/1786776556.sh:15**
* Using `sudo` inside a migration can block or fail in non-interactive runs (e.g., when migrations are applied automatically). Prefer requiring the migration runner to execute as root and call `install` directly, or use `sudo -n` and fail with a clear message if elevation isn’t available.
```
sudo install -D -m 0644 "$source_rule" "$rule"
```
**test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh:32**
* This reads the same small file three times and relies on `&&/||` chaining for control flow. Consider collapsing to a single assertion (e.g., one `grep -Fq` for a combined substring that includes all three properties, or grouping the multi-grep with `{ ...; } || fail ...`) to make the test easier to read and less error-prone.
```
grep -Fq 'ID_VENDOR_ID}=="05ac"' "$touchpad_rule" &&
  grep -Fq 'ID_MODEL_ID}=="0340"' "$touchpad_rule" &&
  grep -Fq 'ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD}=="1"' "$touchpad_rule" ||
  fail "T2 touchpad rule is limited to the affected Apple touchpad"
```
</details>

## Pull request overview

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated no new comments.




<details>
<summary>Suppressed comments (2)</summary>

**test/shell.d/t2-hardware-test.sh:37**
* These assertions only inspect source text; they never execute either new installation path. In particular, the migration can fail to copy the rule, omit `reboot-required`, or lose idempotence/non-T2 behavior while this test still passes because it checks only the hardware-regex string. Add overridable target paths and execute the new migration with the existing `lspci`/`sudo` harness for T2, rerun, and non-T2 cases.
```
grep -Fq 'install -D -m 0644' "$fix_t2" &&
  grep -Fq '99-omarchy-apple-t2-touchpad.rules' "$fix_t2" ||
  fail "fresh T2 setup installs the touchpad integration rule with fixed permissions"
grep -Fq '106b:180[12]' "$touchpad_migration" ||
  fail "T2 touchpad migration is limited to T2 hardware"
```
**default/udev/apple-t2-touchpad.rules:7**
* The PR description says this rule is limited to Apple `05ac:0340`, but this pattern also matches `0278`, `027a`–`027f`, and `0280`. Please either narrow the rule to the documented device or update the description and validation to establish that the broader IDs are intentionally in scope; currently the claimed and implemented device scopes differ.
```
ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="input", KERNEL=="event*", ENV{ID_VENDOR_ID}=="05ac", ENV{ID_MODEL_ID}=="0278|027[a-f]|0280|0340", ENV{ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD}=="1", ENV{ID_INTEGRATION}="internal", ENV{ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION}="internal"
```
</details>

inline.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+# The T2 BCE driver exposes the built-in MacBook touchpad over a virtual USB
+# bus, causing systemd's input_id helper to classify it as external. Mark only
+# the touchpad interface as internal so libinput can enable disable-while-typing.
+ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="input", KERNEL=="event*", ENV{ID_VENDOR_ID}=="05ac", ENV{ID_MODEL_ID}=="0340", ENV{ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD}=="1", ENV{ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION}="internal"
inline.body: `ENV{ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION}="internal"` is assignable and could still be overridden by later rules if any exist after this one (or by unexpected ordering). For a “force final value” override, udev best practice is to use `:=` (final assignment) for properties you need to ensure stay set, e.g. `ENV{ID_INPUT_TOUCHPAD_INTEGRATION}:="internal"`. This makes the override more robust and aligns with the intent of ensuring libinput sees the device as internal.

inline.body: Using `cp` here makes file mode/ownership dependent on `cp` behavior and the runtime umask. To ensure consistent permissions (and match the migration’s approach), prefer `install -D -m 0644` to write into `/etc/udev/rules.d/99-omarchy-apple-t2-touchpad.rules`. This reduces variability across environments and makes the fresh-install path consistent with the migration.

inline.body: The migration explicitly notes libinput must reopen the device and sets `reboot-required`, but the fresh-install path installs the same rule without triggering a reload/reenumeration or marking a reboot required. If `fix-t2.sh` can run on an already-booted system (not only during image build/chroot), users may not see the change take effect until a reboot/session restart. Consider either reloading and triggering udev rules (and/or restarting the relevant stack) or marking `reboot-required` here as well for consistent operational behavior.
